newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - APRIL 16.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - APRIL 16.

text.p: LIDOVE NOVINY - Today the cabinet should announce the contents of its package of economic measures. President Vaclav Havel called on the Social Democrats (CSSD) to support the package, but CSSD is wondering whether it can support the measures.

- According to polls from March, 23.7 percent of voters would vote for the opposition Social Democratic Party, 22.1 percent for the largest coalition party, the Civic Democratic Party and 13.4 percent for the Civic Democratic Alliance.

- The American company Internet Directory for Exporters and Importers (IDEI) is offering Czech businesses free registration on web pages to present their products and to aid them in finding business partners.

- The National Property Fund confirmed yesterday that Salomon Brothers, the financial consultant for privatising IPB bank, should choose several investors interested in the state's stake in IPB this month.

HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - The governer of the Czech National Bank, Josef Tosovsky criticised the activities of the EBRD bank in the Czech Republic last year and called on the bank to participate in privatisation of major Czech banks.
- Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus met with the chairman of the EU commission, Jacques Santer, yesterday. Santer commended the contents of the Czech cabinet's economic measures.
- Komercni Banka announced yesterday that, as the primary manager, it succeeded in placing new bonds from Konsolidacni Banka on the market, which are payable in 2004.
- Aga Gas s.r.o., part of the Swedish company Aga AB, will sign an agreement in Prague today with Skoda Plzen a.s. for cooperative work in optimalising technological processes using technical gases.

MLADA FRONTA DNES - The estimate from experts that the state's expenses must be cut by 25 billion crowns was indirectly confirmed by Finance Minister Ivan Kocarnik. Wages in the public sector should increase by seven percent, not 12.5 percent as the cabinet originally promised.
- The Trade Ministry decided to present a proposal to the cabinet to sell all regional railway lines, about 30 percent of the railway network, which are making the largest losses for Czech Railways.
- The crown fluctuated yesterday and for a short time fell to a 14 month low, but in the end it closed at 1.45 percent below parity.
- Skoda Mlada Boleslav manufactured a total of 82,734 vehicles during the first three months of this year, a year-on-year increase of 18 percent.
PRAVO - On Tuesday, a regional commercial court announced the bankruptcy of Bohemia Art, the majority owner of Poldi Steel.

- If the Slovak Airport Administration does not prolong permission for employees of Slovak Air Services s.r.o., a subsidiary of Czech Airlines (CSA), to enter the Bratislava airport, CSA is prepared to cancel its flights to Bratislava.
